conventions.convention: The proved residual model uses real-valued functions, affine conforming zero-boundary P1 spaces, A=I, constant convection b, and exact weak and Galerkin equations. The variable-diffusion extension supplies notation only.

J_E is the sum of the two outward normal fluxes; the residual representation subtracts J_E. Each cell receives half of an interior-edge estimator contribution. Oscillation uses the cellwise L2 projection onto constants.

Compatible initial 2D labels are assumed. A generation-g triangle has edge labels (g+1,g+1,g), with the unique g edge designated reference. Operational identifiers persist across calls without resetting geometric generations.

Bulk fractions apply to squared contributions. Marking uses the shortest descending-weight prefix, breaking ties by persistent identifier; zero total weight gives empty marks. Three generations are requested on the bulk union and its original edge neighbors. Budget exhaustion rolls back the tentative refinement.
The moment interpolant uses a dual affine volume moment on one selected incident cell at each interior vertex and zero boundary coefficients; it does not evaluate arbitrary H1 functions at vertices.

The convection dual-pickup estimate is an additional sequence hypothesis, not an automatic polygon regularity theorem. Quasi-orthogonality requires μ=C_D h_0^s |b|<1; contraction additionally requires μ/(1−μ)<κ.

The approximation class uses best energy approximation with budget #T−#T_0≤N and weight (N+1)^s. The optimal-complexity theorem is restricted to b=0, initial-cellwise constant data, 0<s≤1/2, sufficiently small estimator bulk fraction, and completed refinement calls.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated constant-convection P1 model, energy error squared is bounded by C_rel η², and each cell indicator is bounded by local error energy plus oscillation. If the fine mesh contains three uniform generations on the original edge-neighbor patch of M, η(U,M)² is bounded by correction energy plus oscillation on that patch, uniformly in the refinement level.

Recursive reference-edge closure of any finite marked set terminates and produces a matching conforming NVB descendant. For three-generation request sets Q_k, #T_n−#T_0≤C_gen Σ#Q_k; the algorithm's edge-neighbor expansion gives #T_n−#T_0≤C_cl Σ#M_k.

The moment interpolant maps H_0^1 into V(T), reproduces V(T), and satisfies local L2 approximation, gradient stability, and interior-edge trace estimates with constants depending only on shape regularity.

For any compatible 2D initial labeling, every conforming NVB descendant has shape regularity bounded in terms of the initial mesh. Three complete uniform generations split every original edge at its midpoint, create an interior median midpoint, and give child diameters at most half the parent diameter.
For nested conforming P1 meshes with exact Galerkin solutions U,U_*, correction energy satisfies ||∇(U_*−U)||²≤C Σ_{K∈R}η_K(U)², where R consists of the coarse cells subdivided in the fine mesh.

For b=0 and initial-cellwise constant f, a comparison mesh reducing energy error by λ produces a Dörfler set on the subdivided overlay cells with parameter θ_*=(1−λ²)/(C_loc C_eff). For 0<θ_E≤min(1,θ_*), the deterministic minimum-cardinality mark has size at most #T_*−#T_0.

With exact solves and completed three-generation calls, energy error squared plus a positive oscillation weight contracts linearly. The symmetric branch needs no initial-mesh smallness; the constant-convection branch assumes uniform dual pickup, μ<1 and μ/(1−μ)<κ. A separately weighted estimator can also be included in the contracting quasi-error.

concerns.concern: The reference-picture prose says, “The eight leaves and their coordinates are verified in proof step 2.1.” The explicit eight leaf triples and midpoint coordinates occur in step 3.1; step 2.1 proves shape regularity.
